title: Gradient Depths
subtitle: Bauhaus thinking applied to something it rarely touched — pure, soft gradient.

tiles: Studying Bauhaus form and minimal color
challenge: Bauhaus tends to live in hard edges and primary color, but the more I read, the more I wanted to see what happened if I took its discipline and pointed it at something soft — pure gradient, no hard forms at all. Could the same thinking still produce something that felt considered?
approach: I read into Bauhaus color theory and the minimalist tradition that grew out of it, then drafted many variations where the whole composition was carried by transitions in value and hue. I kept the ones where the gradient alone felt like enough.
result: A small set of very quiet pieces that I like living with — calm, deep, a little meditative. They're available as prints in case anyone else enjoys the same kind of quiet.
